questions.q: What is the chemical name and formula of 'alum', a substance commonly used in water purification as a coagulant?
questions.a: Potassium aluminium sulfate, with the formula $KAl(SO_4)_2 \cdot 12H_2O$. A wrong answer indicates confusion with common salt or washing soda, revealing a failure to recall specific chemical compounds used in daily water treatment.

questions.q: Why is chlorination preferred over boiling as a large-scale public water disinfection method in municipal water supply systems?
questions.a: Chlorination provides a residual disinfecting effect that protects water throughout distribution pipelines, whereas boiling only kills pathogens present at the moment of heating and leaves water vulnerable to recontamination. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks boiling is practical for entire cities, missing the concept of continuous chemical protection in public infrastructure.

questions.q: A municipal water treatment plant tests raw river water and finds high turbidity due to suspended clay particles. If 50 mg of alum ($KAl(SO_4)_2 \cdot 12H_2O$) is added per liter of water, what primary physical and chemical action does the alum perform to clear the turbidity?
questions.a: Alum dissolves to release aluminium ions ($Al^{3+}$) which neutralize the negative electrical charges on suspended clay colloids, causing them to aggregate into larger flocs that settle rapidly by gravity (sedimentation). A wrong answer reveals a misunderstanding of coagulation, often mistaking it for simple filtration or chemical neutralization of acids.

questions.q: Analyze the role of pH in the effectiveness of chlorine disinfection in public water supplies. Why might highly alkaline water reduce the disinfecting efficiency of chlorine gas ($Cl_2$)?
questions.a: When chlorine dissolves in water, it forms hypochlorous acid ($HOCl$), which is the active germicidal agent, and hydrochloric acid ($HCl$). In alkaline (high pH) water, $HOCl$ dissociates into hypochlorite ions ($OCl^-$), which have significantly lower disinfection efficiency than un-dissociated $HOCl$. A wrong answer shows a lack of awareness of how chemical equilibrium and pH alter the chemical species responsible for pathogen destruction.

questions.q: Evaluate whether adding common salt ($NaCl$) to turbid pond water can serve as an effective substitute for alum in municipal water coagulation. Justify your answer chemically.
questions.a: Adding $NaCl$ is not an effective substitute because sodium ($Na^+$) is a monovalent ion, whereas aluminium ($Al^{3+}$) is trivalent. According to the Schulze-Hardy rule in colloid chemistry, multivalent ions ($Al^{3+}$) are vastly more effective at neutralizing colloidal charges than monovalent ions ($Na^+$). A wrong answer indicates confusion between ionic charge valence and simple solute addition.

questions.q: Design a simple four-step community water purification procedure using household materials to make muddy well water safe for drinking in a rural Indian village.
questions.a: The procedure should include: (1) Coagulation using crushed alum to settle suspended mud; (2) Sedimentation allowing flocs to settle; (3) Filtration through layers of fine sand, coarse gravel, and charcoal to remove residual particles; (4) Disinfection by boiling or adding measured chlorine tablets. A poor answer lacks chemical sequence, such as trying to filter before settling or omitting disinfection.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Public health measures encompass community-level chemical and biological ______ such as safe water purification, proper sewage disposal, and environmental sanitation to prevent the spread of infectious pathogens and chemical contaminants.
Fill in the blank: Observe how turbid rainwater collected in a bucket during the monsoon ______ cloudy even after sitting for hours.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can explain the chemical principles behind water purification methods (sedimentation, coagulation, chlorination), analyze the role of sanitation in preventing chemical and biological contamination of water tables, and evaluate community hygiene practices.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Observe how turbid ______ collected in a bucket during the monsoon remains cloudy even after sitting for hours.
